title: INCLUSION FINANCIERE DES IMMIGRES SUBSAHARIENS AU MAROC : ROLE DES INNOVATIONS FINANCIERES ET ENJEUX D'INTEGRATION SOCIO-ECONOMIQUE
summary: L’inclusion financière constitue un levier important de l’intégration socio-économique des populations immigrées, notamment dans des contextes marqués par des contraintes administratives, informationnelles et institutionnelles. Cette recherche analyse les conditions d’inclusion financière des immigrés subsahariens au Maroc en mettant l’accent sur le rôle des innovations financières, notamment les services bancaires numériques, les paiements mobiles et les solutions FinTech. L’étude adopte une approche méthodologique mixte combinant des entretiens semi-directifs auprès des principales parties prenantes et une enquête quantitative menée auprès d’immigrés subsahariens résidant au Maroc. L’analyse quantitative mobilise des statistiques descriptives, une analyse factorielle exploratoire, des corrélations et une analyse économétrique des déterminants de l’accès aux services financiers numériques. Les résultats montrent que 65 % des répondants disposent d’un compte bancaire au Maroc, tandis que les paiements mobiles et les services bancaires en ligne connaissent une utilisation relativement importante. Toutefois, plusieurs obstacles persistent, notamment la complexité des démarches administratives, les difficultés de compréhension des documents financiers, les barrières linguistiques, le coût des services et un niveau de confiance encore limité envers les institutions financières. L’analyse qualitative confirme l’importance de ces contraintes et met en évidence le rôle potentiel des associations et des acteurs financiers dans l’accompagnement des immigrés. Les résultats suggèrent ainsi que les innovations financières peuvent constituer un levier d’inclusion, mais que leur contribution dépend de leur accessibilité, de leur coût, de leur intelligibilité et de leur adaptation aux besoins spécifiques des utilisateurs. L’étude formule plusieurs recommandations portant sur la simplification des procédures, la communication multilingue, le renforcement de la confiance, le développement de produits financiers adaptés et la coordination entre institutions financières, associations et pouvoirs publics.

title: Sukuk and green bonds in the context of sustainable finance: an empirical analysis
summary: Purpose As the climate crisis intensifies, the transition toward a sustainable economy has become increasingly urgent. This study investigates the dynamic interconnections between Islamic financial instruments, specifically sukuk differentiated by credit ratings, and sustainable finance assets, namely green bonds and clean energy indices. It aims to assess the degree of convergence between Islamic finance and sustainable finance frameworks and to evaluate whether sukuk can contribute to environmental objectives while offering diversification benefits to investors. Design/methodology/approach This study uses an empirical framework based on daily data covering the period from April 30, 2015, to May 1, 2025. The Quantile-on-Quantile (QonQ) methodology is used to capture heterogeneous dependence structures across different market conditions, allowing for the identification of nonlinear and asymmetric relationships across the entire conditional distribution. Sukuk are classified according to credit ratings (AAA, AA, A and BBB) to examine heterogeneous linkages with green bonds and clean energy markets. The results are further illustrated using three-dimensional surface plots. Findings The empirical results show that highly rated sukuk (AAA and AA) exhibit weak and nonlinear dependence with green bonds, indicating limited integration across market conditions. In contrast, lower-rated sukuk (A and BBB) display relatively stronger and more state-dependent relationships, suggesting higher sensitivity to developments in sustainable finance markets. The interactions with clean energy indices remain generally weak and unstable, reflecting limited and heterogeneous integration. Overall, the findings suggest a partial and asymmetric convergence between Islamic finance and sustainable finance systems. Practical implications The results provide relevant insights for investors, policymakers, regulators and Islamic financial institutions. Investors may benefit from including sukuk particularly lower-rated instruments in diversified portfolios alongside sustainable assets to enhance risk-adjusted returns. Policymakers and regulators may use these findings to promote deeper financial integration and support the development of sustainable Islamic finance instruments such as green sukuk. Islamic financial institutions and issuers can leverage these insights to design innovative Shariah-compliant products aligned with sustainability objectives. Originality/value This study provides novel empirical evidence on the nonlinear and asymmetric relationships between sukuk, green bonds and clean energy markets using the QonQ approach. It contributes to the literature by incorporating credit rating heterogeneity and highlighting the conditional nature of interdependence across market states. The results advance the understanding of the convergence between Islamic finance and sustainable finance frameworks.

title: Engineering appetite: commercial framing, ultra-processed products, and the information environment in Nigeria and Uganda
summary: This study examines how commercial framing surrounding ultra-processed products (UPPs) and fast-food chains shape the information environment in Nigeria and Uganda. A qualitative multi-method research design was employed, integrating document review, structured observation of outdoor and point of sale advertising, radio monitoring, digital content analysis, and spatial mapping. Utilizing the Information Environment Assessment (IEA) framework, the study examined how commercial actors structure meaning, visibility, and policy discourse across interconnected domains of People and Community; Information Sources; Actors; and Policy, Process, and Enablers. Guided by critical anthropology and the Commercial Determinants of Health (CDoH), the analysis positions media manipulation as a form of epistemic governance embedded in broader political-economic systems. Data were collected from August 2025 to January in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Kampala and Entebbe. The study comprised 82 purposively selected policy, academic, and corporate documents; 312 outdoor and point-of-sale advertisements; 96 h of radio broadcasting (148 advertisements); 420 digital promotional artifacts from Instagram, Facebook; and spatial mapping of 214 fast-food outlets. In total, 1,164 units were thematically coded using an Information Environment Assessment (IEA) framework across People and community, Information Sources, Actors, and Policy, Process, and enablers. The multimethod approach enabled triangulation of findings across documentary, media, digital, and spatial sources. Findings demonstrate recurring commercial framing through aspirational urban identity, moderation rhetoric, billboard saturation, sports sponsorship, influencer promotion, health-halo packaging, corporate social responsibility campaigns, and economic narratives in policy discourse. The study highlights the importance of examining food related information environment as interconnected system rather than isolated communication channels.

title: The Effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on The Financial Sustainability Of MSMES in Medan City
summary: This study examines the effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on the Financial Sustainability of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Medan City. An associative quantitative design was applied to a survey of 120 MSME owners and managers in the culinary, fashion, retail trade, and service sectors, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met all validity and reliability criteria. Fintech Adoption had a positive and significant effect on Financial Sustainability (β = 0.412; t = 4.873; p < 0.001), and Digital Accounting also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.358; t = 4.126; p < 0.001). Together, the two variables explained 43.4% of the variance in Financial Sustainability, with medium effect sizes (f² = 0.236 and 0.178, respectively). The findings suggest that digital financial services and digital bookkeeping reinforce MSME financial sustainability, so support programs in Medan should promote both together rather than treating them as separate agendas

title: Tariff Uncertainty and Climate Imperatives: Strategies for Supply Chain Decarbonization in Asia
summary: As low-carbon manufacturing accelerates, Asian export economies face growing pressure from cross-border carbon rules and unilateral trade tariffs. Mechanisms such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), together with rising protectionism, have made supply chain emissions central to market access and competitiveness. This paper examines how tariff volatility interacts with climate mandates across Asian production networks and assesses three strategies: carbon-pricing alignment, regional value chain integration, and clean energy deployment in industrial clusters. It finds that without shared carbon accounting standards and transition finance; fragmented border measures may widen industrial disparities between advanced and developing Asian economies. The study highlights the need for cooperative trade-climate frameworks that balance competitiveness with deep decarbonisation across ASEAN and South East Asia.

title: Board Independence, Ownership Structure and Sustainability Reporting: Evidence from East African Listed Firms
summary: This study examined whether board independence moderated the association between ownership structure and sustainability reporting among non-financial listed firms in four East African Community capital markets. The analysis considered managerial ownership, foreign ownership, ownership concentration and institutional ownership. Problem: Prior research has reported inconsistent ownership–disclosure relationships and has often treated board independence as an isolated governance attribute rather than a condition shaping shareholder monitoring. Evidence simultaneously covering multiple ownership categories and East African markets remains limited. Methodology: The study applied a positivist, explanatory longitudinal design using publicly available corporate reports and websites for 51 listed firms in Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda between 2015 and 2024, producing 510 firm-year observations. Sustainability reporting was measured through an economic, environmental and social disclosure index based on Global Reporting Initiative principles. Random-effects panel regression incorporated ownership variables, board independence, firm size, leverage and four ownership-by-independence interactions. Findings: Board independence was positively associated with sustainability reporting in the model without interactions (reported coefficient = 0.3240, p < .001). All four interactions were positive in the final model: managerial ownership (0.2708, p = .010), foreign ownership (0.4549, p < .001), ownership concentration (0.5657, p < .001) and institutional ownership (0.1064, p = .002). The overall R² was .5011. These estimates show conditional associations, not proof that independent directors caused disclosure improvements. Conclusion: Board independence was a consistent positive moderator of the relationships between the four ownership categories and disclosure extent. The results highlight the value of examining ownership and board oversight jointly in governance research and offer evidence relevant to boards, investors and market regulators. Interpretation remains constrained by observational data, reporting-based measurement and unverified model specification details. Keywords: board independence; sustainability reporting; ownership structure; managerial ownership; foreign ownership; institutional ownership; East African Community

title: The Influence of Islamic Capital Market Education and Literacy on Students’ Investment Activity in Digital Sharia Investment Platforms
summary: Despite the growing number of students with sharia investment accounts, active participation in digital Islamic investment platforms remains limited indicating a gap between financial education and actual investment behavior. This study examines the influence of Islamic capital market education and literacy on students’ investment activity on digital sharia platforms. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 95 students in the fifth and seventh semesters of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business (FEBI) at UIN North Sumatra, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. The results show that Islamic capital market education has a positive but statistically non-significant effect on investment activity (β = 0.415; t = 1.726; Sig = 0.088). In contrast, Islamic capital market literacy has a positive and significant effect (β = 0.717; t = 3.274; Sig = 0.001), making it the most dominant predictor (standardized β = 0.463). Simultaneously, both variables significantly explain 46.5% of the variation in investment activity (F = 39.997; Sig= 0.000). These findings suggest that improving applied literacy not merely theoretical education is essential to stimulate active investment behavior, with practical implications for curriculum design, investment gallery programs, and Islamic fintech platform development targeting university students..

title: Incremental value relevance of ESG disclosure: heterogeneous effects across ESG dimensions under crisis conditions in Indonesian mining firms
summary: This study examines whether Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure provides incremental value-relevant information to equity markets and whether its relevance varies across ESG dimensions and crisis conditions. Drawing on competing theoretical mechanisms, the study argues that ESG disclosure does not generate a universally positive valuation effect because informational, stakeholder, legitimacy, institutional, and cost-related mechanisms may operate simultaneously. Using a balanced panel of 30 mining firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange over 2018–2023, the study applies an Ohlson-based price regression to assess the incremental value relevance of ESG disclosure beyond conventional accounting information and firm-level controls. The analysis further disaggregates ESG into environmental, social, and governance dimensions and examines crisis-related changes in their valuation relevance. The findings show that aggregate ESG disclosure does not provide significant incremental value relevance. However, substantial heterogeneity emerges across dimensions: environmental disclosure shows positive incremental value relevance, social disclosure shows negative incremental value relevance, and governance disclosure shows positive incremental value relevance. Moreover, crisis conditions significantly weaken the incremental value relevance of ESG disclosure. These findings demonstrate that ESG value relevance is heterogeneous and crisis-sensitive, with aggregate measures potentially obscuring offsetting effects across ESG dimensions.

title: Earnings Management and Artificial Intelligence Technology Disclosure: Empirical Evidence from a Corporate Impression Management Perspective
summary: While artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly emerged as a technological narrative in capital markets, the descriptions of AI use in corporate annual reports can be real or might be used strategically for image building purposes. Based on A-share listed companies in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2013 to 2023, this study considers whether or not financial embellishment also happens in technological narrative disclosure. The findings reveal that disclosure of AI-related technologies is associated with the level of earnings management of the firm. The result is still strong after the separation of the two types of earnings management (upward and downward). This relationship further found to be influenced by ownership structure and is more strongly observed in non-state owned enterprises. The results indicate that disclosure of AI technology does not necessarily contain only incremental information; it can also serve as a story tool to embellish earnings and build a new image of the company's growth and innovation by companies that manage their earnings. This paper builds on the literature on corporate impression management and offers practical implications for investors and regulators for the evaluation of credibility of narrative disclosures regarding new technologies.

title: Leasing as a Corporate Financing Strategy from a Management Accounting Perspective: A Literature Review Following the Implementation of PSAK 73 (PSAK 116)
summary: The increasing demand for productive assets has encouraged companies to adopt leasing as an alternative financing strategy that supports business expansion without requiring substantial initial capital investment. The implementation of PSAK 73, which was renumbered as PSAK 116 effective January 1, 2024, has transformed lease accounting by requiring the recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities in the statement of financial position, thereby affecting liquidity, capital structure, and corporate financial performance. This study aims to analyze leasing as a corporate financing strategy from a management accounting perspective using a literature review approach. The data were obtained from accounting standards, academic books, and national and international scholarly publications published between 2020 and 2025. The analysis was conducted through the identification, classification, synthesis, and interpretation of literature discussing lease-versus-buy analysis, Net Present Value (NPV), Net Advantage to Leasing (NAL), cash flow analysis, capital structure, and the implications of PSAK 116 implementation. The findings indicate that leasing enhances financing flexibility, maintains liquidity, and optimizes the allocation of corporate financial resources. However, the recognition of lease liabilities under PSAK 116 may increase leverage and influence the interpretation of profitability ratios. This study concludes that leasing is a strategic financing instrument that supports financial planning, investment decision-making, and sustainable corporate financial risk management.

title: Beyond compliance: how voluntary environmental certification drives corporate green innovation in China?
summary: Green manufacturing acts as a core driver for advancing the low-carbon transition of development patterns and fostering emerging industrial growth. Drawing on Porter’s hypothesis, this study exploits the Green Factory Certification (GFC) pilot legislation as an external shock to assess its impact on green technology innovation, employing a multi-period propensity score matching difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) approach. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms spanning 2010 to 2023, this study confirms that the GFC strongly promotes corporate green innovation. The paths of influence include increasing media coverage, attracting green investors, and raising managerial environmental awareness. The above finding still holds after multiple rigorous reliability checks. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that policy effects are especially noticeable in State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), capital-intensive firms, high-tech companies, politically connected entities, and enterprises with non-traditional industrial foundations. Interestingly, while GFC helps enhance corporate value, it has negative spillover effects at the industry level. The study’s conclusions demonstrate how voluntary environmental regulations encourage corporate green innovation, which helps to increase the adoption of sustainable manufacturing practices.

title: From Fragmented Sectors To An Integrated Islamic Economic Ecosystem In Indonesia : A Thematic Literature Review Of Strategic Challanges and Policy Priorities
summary: Abstract. Indonesia’s Islamic economy encompasses Islamic finance, halal industries, micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), digital services, and Islamic social finance. However, these sectors require stronger coordination to create an integrated ecosystem. This article examines the structural challenges and policy priorities associated with strengthening Indonesia’s Islamic economic ecosystem. It employs a qualitative thematic literature review of scholarly publications from 2020 to 2025, complemented by official policy reports. Seven themes are examined: financial literacy and inclusion, productive Islamic financing, halal value-chain integration, MSME capacity and certification, digital transformation, zakat and waqf, and governance and sustainability. The synthesis indicates that financing access alone is insufficient without market access, business capabilities, digital readiness, and an understanding of Sharia contracts. Digital communication can support customer trust and market access, but it does not automatically resolve financial literacy barriers. The article proposes a conceptual framework connecting these components through coordinated governance, institutional collaboration, and policy priorities oriented toward sustainable economic development.

title: Navigating digital disruptions: a supply chain cyber risk and resilience framework
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop an emergent supply chain cyber risk and resilience (SCCRR) framework, grounded in supply chain network theory (SCNT), to identify and prioritise critical cyber supply chain risks and critical resilience-enabling factors. Design/methodology/approach A multiple-case study methodology was adopted across four organisations operating in the food, pharmaceutical and logistics sectors. The framework integrates insights from extant literature and generative AI-assisted exploratory analysis. Qualitative data were analysed using template analysis, while quantitative prioritisation used multi-criteria decision-making techniques. Cross-case analysis enhanced analytical robustness and generalisability. Findings The results identify key strategies for strengthening SCCRR adoption, including integrating cybersecurity practices into supply chain operations, enhancing cross-sector collaboration for threat intelligence sharing and deploying advanced monitoring systems to detect vulnerabilities. The findings further reveal that organisations with lower levels of SCCRR integration exhibit weaker adaptive capacity, highlighting areas where targeted investments, such as vendor audit protocols, crisis management training, and decentralised security architectures, deliver the most significant network-wide benefits. Research limitations/implications The study provides managers with actionable, decision-support insights to prioritise cyber resilience investments across supply networks. The framework supports evidence-based decision-making by linking cyber risks, resilience capabilities and strategic interventions. Originality/value This research advances SCNT-based resilience theory by operationalising cyber risk and resilience through an empirically grounded, decision-oriented framework. It contributes to practice-relevant supply chain research by translating theory-driven network analysis into implementable managerial tools within real-world organisational contexts.

title: Product Innovation and SME Performance: The Roles of Strategic Orientations and IT Utilization in Batik SMEs
summary: This study explores how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in traditional cultural sectors—like Trusmi's batik industry—balance cultural preservation with market adaptation and digital transformation. Prior research often views market orientation, entrepreneurial orientation, and IT utilization as direct performance drivers, but their mechanisms—especially in culturally rooted industries—remain understudied. The research highlights product innovation as a critical intermediary, linking these three capabilities to performance. It examines whether IT enhances performance directly or indirectly by fostering innovation. A quantitative survey of 51 batik SMEs in Trusmi, analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4.0), finds that market orientation, entrepreneurial orientation, and IT utilization significantly boost product innovation, which in turn improves performance. Key findings include IT's negative direct effect on performance but a positive indirect effect through innovation, indicating inconsistent mediation. Theoretically, this extends the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Perspective, showing IT's value lies in driving innovation. Practically, batik SMEs should integrate IT into customer value creation rather than adopting it passively. Ultimately, performance depends on SMEs' ability to convert resources—including IT—into innovations that align with market demands. The study emphasizes innovation'​s role as a bridge between capabilities and sustained success in culturally significant industries.

title: Digital Marketing Strategy As A Driving Factor Of Sme Marketing Performance: Literature Review
summary: Digital transformation has transformed the marketing landscape of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in reaching consumers, building brands, and increasing sales. title: Artificial Intelligence, ESG Disclosure Quality, and Corporate Sustainability Performance in Islamic Banking: The Role of Sharia Governance
summary: This study examines the relationships among Artificial Intelligence (AI), ESG Disclosure Quality (ESGDQ), Greenwashing, and Corporate Sustainability Performance (CSP), and investigates the moderating role of Sharia Governance in Islamic banking. The study employs a quantitative explanatory design using panel data from Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia and Malaysia during the 2021–2025 period. The study collected data from annual reports, sustainability reports, corporate governance reports, official corporate websites, and other publicly available disclosures through structured content analysis and disclosure-based indices. The hypotheses were tested using a fixed-effects panel regression model. The findings indicate that disclosed AI capability and implementation are positively associated with ESG Disclosure Quality, while AI is not significantly associated with Greenwashing. ESG Disclosure Quality is positively associated with Corporate Sustainability Performance, whereas Greenwashing is not significantly associated with sustainability performance. Sharia Governance strengthens the positive relationship between AI and ESG Disclosure Quality but does not significantly moderate the relationship between AI and Greenwashing. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with Sharia Governance to support more credible, transparent, and responsible sustainability reporting practices in Islamic banking.

title: Digital Brand Experience and Reputation Building In Sustainable Urban Mobility
summary: Digital transformation has accelerated the adoption of sustainable urban mobility, yet limited evidence explains how technological quality translates into sustainable mobility through user experience and reputation, particularly in emerging Indonesian cities. This study investigates the effects of system quality, information quality, and eco-efficiency on digital brand experience and examines the mediating roles of digital brand experience and reputation quotient in enhancing resilience and sustainable urban mobility. A quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) was employed. Data were collected from 360 valid users of digital mobility applications in Lampung, Palembang, and Medan and analyzed using SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that system quality (β = 0.281), information quality (β = 0.302), and eco-efficiency (β = 0.268) significantly improve digital brand experience. Digital brand experience positively influences reputation quotient (β = 0.546), which subsequently strengthens resilience (β = 0.429) and sustainable urban mobility (β = 0.357). In addition, digital brand experience directly enhances sustainable urban mobility (β = 0.284). Mediation analysis confirms that digital brand experience and reputation quotient partially mediate the relationship between technological quality and sustainable mobility outcomes. The findings demonstrate that technological performance contributes to sustainable urban mobility primarily through positive user experiences and strong organizational reputation, extending the Information Systems Success Model, Brand Experience Theory, and Reputation Quotient framework.

title: The Impact Mechanism and Implementation Path of Green Human Resource Management on the ESG Performance of Enterprises
summary: In the context of the comprehensive green transformation of economic and social development and the significant attention paid by the capital market to ESG values, relying on the internal human resource system to drive the sustainable development of enterprises has become an important research topic. Based on the stakeholder theory, this paper selects green human resource management and the ESG performance of enterprises as the research objects, and uses the mechanism analysis method to explore the intrinsic relationship between the two. The research findings show that green human resource practices can enhance the environmental performance, social performance, and governance performance of enterprises through three paths, and the effect is constrained by industry and property rights characteristics. It also proposes implementation paths such as establishing a hierarchical and classified green training system and improving the green performance assessment and incentive mechanism. This paper expands the research boundary of ESG influencing factors from the perspective of micro internal human resource management and provides references for enterprises to optimize their green human resource systems and implement sustainable development strategies.

title: Development of lifecycle-based building information modelling (BIM) implementation model for the Sarawak construction industry: an empirical structural equation modelling approach
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop a project lifecycle-based building information modelling (BIM) implementation model in Sarawak and examine the relationships between current practices (CPs) across project lifecycle stages and critical success factors (CSFs) influencing BIM implementation. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire survey was conducted among 295 construction professionals in Sarawak. The collected data were analysed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modelling (SEM) through IBM SPSS Amos to validate the proposed BIM implementation model. Findings The analysis identified three project lifecycle phases (design, procurement and construction) and four CSF dimensions (organizational readiness, human capital and collaboration, external institutional support and technology infrastructure). SEM results revealed significant relationships between project lifecycle and CSFs associated with CPs. Research limitations/implications The findings provide a strategic roadmap for policymakers, industry stakeholders and practitioners by identifying actionable measures to enhance BIM adoption and support digital transformation within Sarawak’s construction industry. Practical implications Theoretically, this study contributes to BIM adoption literature by integrating the CSF approach with the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and empirically validating the relationships through EFA, CFA and SEM. Practically, the proposed model provides policymakers and industry stakeholders with a structured roadmap for prioritizing BIM adoption strategies across the project lifecycle. Originality/value This study extends existing BIM adoption and CSF models by integrating empirically derived, TOE-aligned CSF dimensions with observable CPs across project lifecycle stages. The proposed model evaluates their relationships with BIM implementation practices during the design, procurement and construction/operation stages.

title: A socio-computational framework for evaluating artificial intelligence adoption readiness in small-scale businesses
summary: Purpose Adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) across small-scale businesses remains uneven even with the growing pace of digital transformation. Large enterprises are rapidly integrating AI into their operations, while there is still a barrier to adoption within small-scale businesses. This study proposes and examines an exploratory computational readiness index (CRI) that brings together behavioral, organizational and environmental dimensions to understand the preparedness of small-scale businesses in adopting AI. This index is offered as a preliminary firm-level diagnostic rather than a fully validated measure. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, multi-source design was used, combining primary survey data from small-scale businesses with secondary global data collected from international sources and informal conversations with additional small business owners, managers and employees who fell outside the formal survey sample. Survey instruments were used to capture behavioral, organizational and environmental factors influencing the decision to adopt AI. This was also complemented with secondary global data collected and combined to derive the readiness index. Appropriate statistical tests were conducted to examine relationships among key dimensions and the overall readiness index. Findings Organizational factors like employee skills, motivation and opportunities were most consistently linked with readiness across groups, followed by individuals’ behavioral factors. External factors such as infrastructure and environment appeared to have comparatively smaller influence. The results of the study have been used to develop a readiness index that is intended to indicate the extent to which a small-scale business may be prepared to adopt AI. Practical implications The CRI proposed in this study can become a practical tool for policymakers and leaders within small-scale businesses for readiness assessment, prioritizing capability building within the organization rather than focusing on infrastructure investments alone. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by proposing a novel framework for assessing AI readiness in small-scale businesses, integrating human, organizational and environmental dimensions.

title: Steering sustainability: the configurational role of FinTech in governance-driven emission reduction goals in Islamic and conventional banks
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate how corporate governance influences banks’ emission reduction goals (ERG), focusing on the configurational role of FinTech disclosure. Design/methodology/approach The study examines 20 banks listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange over 2020–2023 (80 bank-year observations), covering both Islamic and conventional banks. It applies fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify configurations of governance attributes, FinTech disclosure and bank characteristics that are sufficient for ERG. Findings The results show that no single governance attribute is sufficient to ensure ERG; instead, ERG emerge from specific configurations of governance features, FinTech disclosure and financial characteristics. Smaller boards, higher proportions of independent and female directors and strong Shariah board presence contribute to ERG when combined with high FinTech disclosure and favorable bank-level conditions. Practical implications The findings provide actionable guidance for regulators and bank boards. Strengthening governance structures (e.g. independent and diverse boards) and encouraging transparent FinTech disclosure can help integrate environmental objectives into governance and digital strategies, especially in emerging markets. Originality/value This study makes three original contributions to the Islamic and conventional banking literature. First, it is, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, the first study to apply fsQCA to the governance–FinTech–sustainability triad in a dual banking system, capturing conjunctural causation, equifinality and causal asymmetry across Islamic and conventional banks – features that are systematically missed by symmetric regression methods. Second, by explicitly modeling Shariah board governance as a core configurational condition alongside conventional board attributes, the study provides novel evidence that Islamic religious–ethical oversight constitutes a distinct and nonsubstitutable governance mechanism for emission reduction commitment, enriching the Shariah governance quality and green Islamic banking literatures. Third, situated in Pakistan’s dual banking system –where the State Bank of Pakistan’s green banking guidelines and Shariah governance framework create overlapping regulatory logics for climate and Islamic governance – the study delivers policy relevant configurational insights for Islamic banking regulators across South Asia and the Gulf Cooperation Council who are navigating the twin imperatives of digital transformation and climate risk governance.

title: The impact of Generation Z on the Workplace: A scoping review
summary: Abstract: Orientation: Generation Z (Gen Z) has different communication styles, leadership preferences, job expectations and workplace perceptions. As they enter the workplace, these differences create new challenges for managers and organisations. However, research on their workplace impact remains limited, calling for a synthesis of current evidence. Research purpose: This study adopts a scoping review methodology to map the literature regarding Gen Z employees’ impact on the workplace, present a complete picture of the literature, summarise the evidence, highlight knowledge gaps and provide directions for future research. Motivation for the study: Generation Z has become a large part of the workforce. They may reshape workplace practices and management approaches. However, a search using relevant strings revealed that no review has specifically synthesised evidence of their impact on the workplace. Research approach/design and method: This study used a scoping review design following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidelines. This approach was used to map existing evidence on Gen Z employees’ impact on the workplace, clarify key concepts and identify research gaps. The review was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses extension for Scoping Reviews checklist. Main findings: This scoping review maps the existing evidence from 38 studies to report Gen Z employees’ impact on the workplace. This study has identified six impact themes, namely communication, leadership and management practices, organisational performance, organisational culture, digital transformation and withdrawal and misconduct. Practical/managerial implications: This review offers practical insights to help organisations manage Gen Z’s workplace impact more effectively. Managers should pay closer attention to the six impacts, so that Gen Z employees’ contribution to workplace change and organisational performance can be better supported. Contribution/value-add: By outlining what has been studied and where evidence remains limited, this review has identified certain research gaps from different perspectives, providing useful guidance for future research.

title: International Evidence on the Relationship Between ESG Decoupling and Earnings Quality
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) decoupling and earnings quality (EQ) using an international sample of firms over the period 2005–2024. ESG decoupling refers to the misalignment between firms' ESG disclosure and ESG performance. The results show that ESG decoupling is negatively associated with EQ, suggesting that greater divergence between what firms communicate about ESG and what they substantively achieve is linked to lower‐quality financial reporting. This finding is consistent with legitimacy theory, which distinguishes between symbolic and substantive organisational behaviour. Further analysis shows that the negative association is stronger in countries with weaker governance quality, indicating that the institutional environment shapes the extent to which ESG misalignment is associated with reporting quality. Additional tests distinguishing between the direction of misalignment reveal that greenwashing is negatively associated with EQ, whereas brownwashing is not significantly associated with EQ. Overall, the findings extend the literature by showing that ESG decoupling is relevant to both the credibility of sustainability reporting and financial reporting quality, and that this association varies across governance settings.

title: T–MEC: los derechos humanos laborales en México rumbo a la revisión de 2026
summary: La revisión del Tratado entre México, Estados Unidos y Canadá (T–MEC) es un proceso asimétrico, que se da en medio de pesos y contrapesos, en el que los gobiernos de los tres países y los sectores empresariales defienden sus intereses. Uno de los temas que se ha puesto en la mesa de debate ha sido el capítulo laboral, en particular del Mecanismo Laboral de Respuesta Rápida (MLRR). Este artículo acerca las voces de las personas trabajadoras y de la sociedad civil organizada, a partir del corpus generado por la Asamblea de Incidencia del T–MEC, dando importancia a los pendientes estructurales (subcontratación, género, migración laboral, cadenas de suministro, entre otros.), así como algunas propuestas que la convergencia civil mexicana, estadounidense y canadiense han impulsado en torno a la revisión del T–MEC. Desde cereal creemos que, sin organización colectiva, sin ampliación de los alcances y sin sanciones efectivas de por medio, el capítulo laboral del T–MEC corre el riesgo de quedarse en letra muerta.

title: Supply Chain Contagion: How Customers’ Abnormal Temperature Exposure Amplifies Suppliers’ Debt Default Risk
summary: Corporate debt defaults are a major source of financial risk and can threaten market stability when they occur on a large scale. Meanwhile, shifts in the global climate and episodes of extreme weather are profoundly altering economies and financial systems. Against this backdrop, examining how temperature-related shocks affect corporate default risk is essential for understanding credit risk transmission under changing environmental conditions. We investigate how customer-side exposure to abnormal temperatures affects suppliers’ debt default risk, using observations for Chinese A-share listed firms over 2008–2023. The findings indicate that suppliers’ debt default risk increases as the annual average temperature in customers’ locations rises further above its long-term historical average. The channel analysis provides evidence consistent with two channels: customers’ abnormal temperature shocks are associated with weaker demand for suppliers’ products and tighter financing conditions, which may help explain the increase in supplier default risk. Heterogeneity tests show that this effect is stronger among suppliers with greater customer dependence or tighter financing constraints, consistent with the demand and financing channels. The effect is also more pronounced for suppliers without green products, whereas stronger ESG performance helps mitigate the adverse impact. Additional analysis links customers’ abnormal temperature exposure to lower subsequent customer concentration among suppliers, suggesting possible adaptation through customer diversification.

title: Applications of operations research techniques in supply chain optimisation
summary: Supply chains involve linked decisions on facility location, production, inventory, routing and supplier choice under limits on capacity, cost and time. This paper reviews seventeen research papers on Operations Research (OR) in supply chains and compares the techniques they use: Linear and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (LP and MILP), metaheuristics (Genetic Algorithm and Tabu Search), Discrete-Event Simulation (DES), Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Markov Decision Processes with Dynamic Programming (MDP and DP) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), together with decomposition methods such as Benders decomposition and Lagrangian relaxation. Each technique is scored on six weighted criteria: decision quality, fit with network decisions, scalability, handling of uncertainty, implementation effort and documented impact. MILP ranks first, because it models yes or no structural choices and continuous flows together and returns optimal or provably near-optimal answers. Its weaknesses, problem size and uncertainty, are addressed in the literature through decomposition, stochastic extensions and simulation. We therefore recommend MILP as the core technique, supported by those tools, and we discuss gaps in the evidence and what we could have done better.

title: The AI SBOM Securing the Supply Chain Beyond the Gateway
summary: Artificial intelligence systems are transforming enterprise infrastructure while expanding the software supply chain attack surface. Traditional Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) track code dependencies, yet AI introduces opaque components that evade conventional visibility: pre-trained model weights, training datasets, fine-tuning pipelines, and GPU-accelerated infrastructure. The AI-SBOM extends existing SBOM practice to capture the provenance, lineage, and security posture of these components. This article consolidates emerging guidance (the G7 minimum elements for AI SBOMs, CISA's 2025 SBOM minimum elements, and the AI extensions of the SPDX and CycloneDX standards) into an actionable taxonomy for the practicing IT professional, introduces a four-level verifiability grading that turns AI-SBOM trustworthiness into a measurable property, pairs both with a phased implementation roadmap grounded in recent supply chain compromises, and assesses the approach's current limitations. title: AI Driven Early Warning of ESG Performance in Real Estate Enterprises
summary: Real estate enterprises face increasing pressure from green transition, financing constraints, and higher requirements for governance transparency. ESG performance has become an important basis for evaluating sustainable operation, risk exposure, and management quality. Due to high leverage, long development cycles, and strong externalities in the real estate industry, ESG performance deterioration often appears together with liquidity risk, weak disclosure, and governance defects. Based on Chinese A-share listed real estate enterprises from 2015 to 2024, ESG ratings, financial indicators, governance variables, and textual information from annual reports and ESG reports are integrated to build an AI-driven early-warning model for ESG performance. TF-IDF is used to extract textual risk signals. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM are compared, while SHAP is applied to explain key driving factors. The results show that LightGBM achieves the highest AUC and F1 score on the test set, indicating stronger ability to identify firms with ESG performance deterioration in the following year. Leverage ratio, cash-to-short-term debt ratio, negative risk-word frequency, environmental disclosure intensity, and governance penalty records are the main influencing factors. This framework can support ESG risk identification, internal governance improvement, and investment risk screening in real estate enterprises.

title: AISDBM-Agent: An LLM-Enabled Autonomous Decision-Making Prototype System for Intelligent Supply Chain Inventory Optimization
summary: The digital transformation of supply chain operations demands manufacturing systems capable of autonomous decision-making in response to dynamic production fluctuations. However, existing inventory management approaches suffer from limited adaptability to plan variations and delayed response times, primarily due to the absence of tight coupling between inventory control and real-time production demand. To address these challenges, this study proposes AISDBM-Agent, an LLM-enabled autonomous decision-making prototype system for intelligent supply chain inventory optimization. The framework is structured into four functional modules: the perception module receives and translates external multi-source information; the memory module integrates, categorizes, and stores the processed information to mitigate the risks arising from outdated knowledge or contextual inconsistencies; the strategy module utilizes the processed input from the perception module and the knowledge provided by the memory module to perform reasoning and decision-making, automatically generating optimal procurement decisions, employing the Chain of Thought (CoT) method to enhance the transparency and interpretability of these decisions; the execution module interacts with external systems and obtains execution feedback to ensure information timeliness, thereby resolving the issue of delayed response in inventory management. A case study on steel scrap inventory management is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that AISDBM-Agent significantly enhances the system’s ability to respond to fluctuations in demand, enabling the smooth management of stock levels.

title: Trust and Adoption Intention Toward AI-Enabled IBM Cloud Services Among IT Professionals in Bangladesh
summary: Artificial-intelligence-enabled cloud services are becoming increasingly important for digital transformation, but users may not adopt these services simply because they believe the technology is useful. This study examines the factors associated with adoption intention toward AI-enabled IBM Cloud services in Bangladesh, with particular attention to performance expectations, trust, technology readiness and digital skills readiness. The analysis uses the Group 5 survey database, which contains 400 records. After applying the prespecified attention-check criterion, 385 cases were retained for the main analysis. The database contains 30 five-point Likert-scale items representing 10 constructs: perceived usefulness, relative advantage, compatibility, innovation adoption readiness, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, trust, technology readiness, digital skills readiness and adoption intention. Descriptive statistics, reliability and measurement diagnostics, hierarchical regression, bootstrap analysis and importance-performance analysis were used to examine the data. Overall adoption intention was positive (M=3.79, SD=0.48). The full regression model explained 30.5% of the variance in adoption intention. Technology readiness was the strongest unique predictor (β=.224, p<.001), followed by performance expectancy (β=.157, p=.001), digital skills readiness (β=.147, p=.002) and trust (β=.140, p=.003). Adding the trust and readiness variables increased the explained variance by 11.6 percentage points (ΔR²=.116), showing that these factors provide important information beyond innovation attributes and UTAUT-oriented expectations. An exploratory indirect pathway was also observed: technology readiness was positively related to digital skills readiness, which was in turn related to adoption intention. The bootstrapped indirect effect was positive (ab=.067, 95% CI [.031, .108]). These findings suggest that AI-enabled cloud adoption is not only a question of perceived technological value; it also depends on whether users feel prepared, digitally capable and sufficiently confident in the cloud provider. However, all ten three-item scales showed Cronbach's alpha values below .70, and several discriminant-validity indicators were elevated. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as data-grounded associations rather than as definitive confirmation of a latent-variable model. The main contribution of the study is a readiness-centered interpretation of AI-enabled cloud adoption in the Bangladesh context, together with a clear recommendation for future scale validation and confirmatory testing.

title: Research on the Influence Mechanism and Effects of Digital Economy on Carbon Emissions from Urban Tourism in China
summary: Amid growing international efforts to address climate change and China's commitment to its carbon peak and carbon neutrality targets, transforming the tourism sector toward low-carbon practices is now critical to advancing sustainable and high-quality economic growth. As a new engine of structural transformation, the digital economy may help address the carbon-intensive growth of the tourism sector, yet its effects and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study examines the impact of China's digital economy on urban tourism carbon emissions using panel data from 282 prefecture-level cities from 2005 to 2023. Results show that the digital economy significantly reduces total tourism carbon emissions but initially increases carbon emission intensity. The relationship between the digital economy and tourism-related carbon emissions follows a nonlinear inverted U-curve pattern. Mechanism analysis reveals three pathways: (1) energy-efficiency improvement through technological innovation, (2) rebound effects driven by market expansion, and (3) structural upgrading through industrial integration. The overall effect therefore depends on the evolving balance between efficiency gains and scale expansion. Regional heterogeneity is also evident: the emission-reduction effect is strongest in eastern China, weaker in central China, and turns positive in western China in the short term. These findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the environmental consequences of digital transformation in tourism and offer policy implications for designing region-specific digital and low-carbon transition strategies.

title: Firm Attributes and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Nonfinancial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The series of corporate failures and reporting irregularities despites the full adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards have raised concerns on factors affecting financial reporting quality in Nigeria. Consequently, the main objective of this study was to investigate the effect of firm attributes on financial reporting quality of listed nonfinancial companies in Nigeria. Specifically, this study examined how auditor type, sustainability disclosure practices, board financial expertise, affect income smoothing. The research design adopted in this study was ex post facto, secondary data were used and the population of the study was 100 listed nonfinancial companies out of which 85 companies were purposively selected as the sample size. The technique of data analysis employed was panel regression analysis and the statistical package used was STATA 17. The findings of the study revealed that auditor type has a positive and statistically significant effect (coeff. = 0.387, p = 0.007); sustainability disclosure practices (SUDP) has a positive but statistically nonsignificant effect(coeff. = 0.525, p = 0.491); and board financial expertise has a positive and statistically significant effect (coeff. = 1.597, p = 0.038) on income smoothing of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria. It was thus concluded that firm attributesare fundamental in reducing income smoothing and enhancing the financial reporting quality among listed non-financial companies in Nigeria. It was therefore recommended amongst others that the management of these firms should strengthen the independence of audit committees to enhance their oversight role and reduce opportunities for earnings manipulation.

title: Government Policy Instruments and Sustainable Supply Chain Management Adoption in Resource-Intensive and High-Impact Industries: A Critical Integrative Review
summary: Government policy is often treated as an external driver of sustainable supply chain management (SSCM), yet policy exposure need not produce durable supplier-facing change. This critical integrative review develops a functional taxonomy of capability-building, coercive enforcement, market-shaping, information-forcing, and orchestration instruments. A retrospective source-critical audit retained 100 full-text publications from an original 103-publication inventory: 96 substantive sources and four methodological anchors. The synthesis distinguishes policy exposure, adoption quality, and downstream sustainability effectiveness. It proposes capability support, enforcement credibility, and observability and verification as potentially complementary conditions, not empirically established necessities. Source-level contrasts show that support can have opposite associations across supplier practices, environmental and financial outcomes can diverge, and improved disclosure need not establish remediation. Resource intensity and high impact are defined at the process and supply-chain level, with six boundary dimensions specifying transfer. Operational proxies and a proposition-specific testing roadmap are provided. The audit supplies design-sensitive limitations and source-page anchors; missing historical search records, single-reviewer interpretation, and heterogeneous measures constrain coverage and causal inference. The contribution is a mechanism-based framework for empirical testing, not a causal ranking of policy instruments.

title: ISHEA REPORT V1 2026
summary: The Physical Limit of Capital: Energy, Infrastructure and Geopolitics in the New Resource Economy ISHEA Premiere Report · Vol. 1, No. 1 · September 2026 This report examines the relationship between financial capital, physical resource availability, infrastructure resilience, and geopolitical risk in the global economy. It explores how the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, the reconfiguration of energy and mineral supply chains, and the strategic transformation of maritime and logistics corridors are reshaping the conditions under which financial value can be converted into realizable economic activity. Using an interdisciplinary analytical framework informed by biophysical accounting, bioenergetics, cognitive economics, complex systems, and resilience analysis, the report examines three interconnected dimensions: the physical infrastructure supporting AI-related investment; the strategic role of energy resources and logistics corridors in international capital allocation; and the implications of geopolitical disruption for asset valuation and business planning. The report introduces an ISHEA analytical heuristic, Realizable Value, which considers financial value alongside physical availability, logistical resilience, and flow security. This formulation is presented as a diagnostic framework rather than a calibrated or empirically validated valuation model. The report concludes with practical recommendations for business planning in 2026–2027, including physical-dependency audits, geographic and supplier redundancy, energy-risk assessment, and systemic stress testing. Purpose: To contribute to interdisciplinary discussion on the relationship between financial valuation and the physical, infrastructural, and geopolitical conditions that sustain economic activity. title: Factors affecting the efficiency of Vietnam's coal export supply chain
summary: This study analyzes the factors affecting the efficiency of Vietnam's coal export supply chain in the context of increasingly coordinated mining, screening, warehousing, port operations, and international trade. Based on supply chain management theory, resource-based and dynamic capability perspectives, the paper examines five groups of factors: logistics infrastructure capacity; information sharing; supply chain cooperation; logistics digitalization; and adaptability to market and institutional conditions. The research results show that the efficiency of the export supply chain is not determined by a single link but depends on the degree of synchronization between the flow of materials, information flow, and coordinated decisions between mining companies, warehousing units, ports, transportation vehicles, and export business units. Among these, logistics infrastructure capacity and supply chain cooperation play a prominent role. Information sharing, logistics digitalization, and adaptability facilitate improved delivery reliability, reduced lead times, cost control, and better responsiveness to international market fluctuations. This research contributes to the evidence-based management of bulk cargo supply chains in the mining industry, while also suggesting implications for synchronizing warehousing, port, and transportation capabilities, increasing data sharing, developing digital coordination platforms, and strengthening inter-unit coordination mechanisms within the coal export chain.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Finance Digitalization on Corporate Working Capital Management Efficiency
summary: As firms face volatile cash flows, tighter external financing, and greater pressure to coordinate financial and operating activities, supply chain finance digitalization is changing how transaction data, financing, payments, and settlement are connected. Existing studies often examine digital supply chain finance through individual financial outcomes or isolated cases, while relatively few systematically consider both its direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms on working capital management efficiency. This paper examines the effect of digital supply chain finance on corporate working capital management efficiency through a structured review and conceptual synthesis of recent literature, with a focus on direct effects and three indirect mechanisms. The evidence suggests that digital supply chain finance improves working capital efficiency by accelerating financing and settlement, reducing unnecessary capital tied up in receivables and inventories, and coordinating receivables, payables, inventories, and cash flows. Overall, the main channels are greater information transparency, better financing access, and closer financial-operational coordination. This paper constructs an analytical framework that incorporates direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms. Thereby contributing to the literature on digitalization in supply chain finance and corporate working capital management.

title: Analysis of the Resilience of China's Fresh Food E-Commerce Supply Chains after COVID-19: Evidence from Hema Fresh
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused severe disruptions to global supply chains, and the fresh food e-commerce sector has been particularly affected due to the perishable nature of its products and the strict time requirements in distribution. Understanding how fresh food e-commerce platforms cope with such extreme shocks and rebuild their supply chains afterwards is therefore of both practical and research significance. This study takes Hema Fresh as a case to examine the disruption risks it encountered during the pandemic, the emergency measures it adopted, and the strategic transformation it pursued in the post-pandemic period. Using a single-case-study approach and drawing on multiple data sources including corporate financial reports, media coverage, academic papers, and industry research reports, the study applies thematic analysis to identify key patterns in Hema's resilience-building process. The findings show that Hema effectively addressed immediate crises through measures such as the "shared employee" program and multi-source procurement, and later achieved a turnaround from loss to profit through discount reforms and vertical supply chain integration. However, the study also identifies a persistent tension between cost efficiency and resilience redundancy, which remains a key challenge for Hema and the broader fresh e-commerce industry.

title: An Analytical Study on Artificial Intelligence as a Turning Point for the Transformation of the Auditing Industry
summary: With the digital economy growing at an unprecedented rate, corporate transaction data has become exponentially large, presenting several challenges to the auditing profession - including the exponential increase in the volume of data, more complex transaction patterns, and stricter regulatory requirements - making traditional sampling-based auditing techniques less effective. This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be a game changer in the evolution of the auditing industry. The research employs both literature review and comparative analysis to provide a systematic account of how AI has been used in the auditing industry since 2015. The analysis is divided into four main dimensions: transformation of auditing processes, motivations behind the adoption of AI, the practical benefits of its implementation, and obstacles faced during this process. The results suggest that AI is radically changing the scope, effectiveness, and decision-making references of the auditing profession, making it one of the key drivers of industry development. Nonetheless, the influence of AI is unfolding slowly; the sector is now in the transitional stage: moving towards a mainly human-oriented strategy to a human-machine partnership. The main issues that should be addressed in this transition are overdependence on AI, the absence of transparency in algorithmic decision-making, the specification of accountability, and the change of the auditing workforce. On the basis of the information provided in this paper, the author suggests practical suggestions on AI governance practices of firms, the creation of strong regulatory frameworks, and the development of competent auditing talent.

title: Technological Advancements and Barriers in Adopting Digital Twins for Supply Chain Management
summary: Digital twins are expected to improve supply chain decisions by linking physical operations with models that simulate and optimize them. This literature review, guided by PRISMA 2020, analyzes 104 studies (2016 to 2026) on the enabling technologies of supply chain digital twins, the barriers to their adoption and the algorithmic evidence behind them. The studies were classified into evidence tiers by application domain; twelve supply chain studies and six algorithm studies from other sectors were coded by decision problem, algorithm family, integration level and validation, and the methodological quality of fifteen of them was appraised. The Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, cloud and edge computing, extended reality and blockchain are the main enablers, but in the analyzed set the supply chain evidence is largely conceptual: only two supply chain studies apply an algorithm, none implements a bidirectional digital twin, and only one reports performance measures from a model run. State estimation, reduced-order models and reinforcement learning, which would allow real-time operation, have been evaluated only in other sectors. Technical, organizational and economic barriers appear to reinforce each other. We propose a three-stage implementation pathway and an agenda of seven research gaps, including closed-loop integration, shared benchmarks and multi-company data governance.

title: Blockchain in Supply Chain Transparency, Flexibility, and Supplier Trust in a Lean Perspective
summary: This study examines to analyze the role of blockchain technology in supporting transparency, flexibility, and supplier trust through Lean Supply Chain techniques at PT Siam Cement Group Yogyakarta. The research employs a qualitative approach, utilizing in-depth narrative interviews and direct observation of the implementation of the RMC NET system. Data were gathered from key informants involved in operational activities and system usage, then analyzed through open coding, categorization, cross-informant comparison, and triangulation. The findings indicate that blockchain enhances information visibility and traceability, cross-functional integration, and decision-making rapidity. These factors foster internal transparency, operational flexibility, and the implementation of a Lean Supply Chain by improving process efficiency, productivity, inventory management, delivery performance, processing time, and quality. However, blockchain has not directly shaped supplier trust, which is instead more significantly influenced by performance track records, consistency, communication, and direct interaction.

title: An Exploratory Impact Studies of Digitalisation on Global Supply Chain Sustainability Practices
summary: In recent years, the realm of decision management research focused on supply chain sustainability has grown significantly and emerged as a highly active and productive area. The foundation of sustainability relies on the concept of innovation. Traditional business practices and environmental responsibility are being transformed by the incorporation of digitalization in supply chain sustainability. title: The North American germanium supply chain: military applications and civilian competition
summary: Germanium is not mined as a primary ore anywhere in North America. It comes out as a trace byproduct of zinc processing, at concentrations low enough that its supply follows the economics of zinc rather than germanium. Additionally, it depends on whether a smelter operator is willing to install a costly recovery circuit on top of ordinary zinc refining. That fact, more than any single company's decision, explains why a metal essential to night vision optics, thermal weapon sights, laser rangefinders, and satellite solar arrays runs through a chain that reduces to a small number of US zinc operations feeding one foreign smelter.

title: Smart Manufacturing Driven Multi-objective Carbon-Constrained Production and Supply Chain Coordination Optimization
summary: The low-carbon transformation of manufacturing makes production planning no longer limited to cost reduction and delivery efficiency, as carbon emissions, energy consumption, and supply chain coordination have become key decision factors in smart manufacturing systems. Focusing on carbon-constrained production and supply chain coordination optimization, a multi-objective optimization framework is constructed by integrating equipment status, machining processes, order delivery, inventory configuration, transportation batching, and carbon emission accounting. The experiment uses open equipment-state data, CNC machining data, and carbon emission factors from 2020 to 2026 to construct reproducible controlled simulation instances. An improved NSGA-II algorithm is applied to obtain Pareto solution sets for cost, makespan, and carbon emissions. The results show that the improved NSGA-II outperforms the standard NSGA-II in total cost, maximum makespan, carbon emissions, Hypervolume, and Spread, while maintaining delivery stability and reducing system-level emissions. These findings indicate that smart manufacturing data-driven coordination optimization can provide computable and comparable decision support for low-carbon production scheduling and supply chain coordination.

title: The Influence of Organizational Culture Factors on the Acceptance of New Accounting Technology Among Accounting Staff in Foreign-Invested Enterprises in Hanoi City
summary: This paper examines the influence of organizational culture factors on the acceptance of new accounting technology among accounting staff in foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises in Hanoi City, using a desk-research approach that combines synthesis, analysis, evaluation, and comparison of the literature. Drawing on Hofstede's theory of organizational culture, the Technology Acceptance Model, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, and Diffusion of Innovation theory, the paper develops a conceptual framework that clarifies the mechanisms through which five dimensions of organizational culture, namely power distance, uncertainty avoidance, individualism and collectivism, long-term and short-term orientation, and masculinity and femininity, affect the components of technology-acceptance behavior. The analysis shows that power distance and uncertainty avoidance play a relatively consistent role in amplifying social influence, while the interplay between parent-company culture and local culture within this type of enterprise adds a further layer of complexity to the digital transformation of accounting. Building on these findings, the paper proposes managerial implications tailored to each cultural dimension for enterprise managers, while also suggesting policy directions through which state management agencies can support digital transformation in the accounting profession.

title: THE IMPACT OF THE POLITICAL DECISION ON THE QUALITY OF FINANCIAL REPORTS IN THE IRAQI BANKING ENVIRONMENT: AN APPLIED STUDY
summary: The study examined the impact of political decisions on the quality of the financial reports of traditional banks in light of the presence of a gap between the information included in the financial reports and the results or effects of the political decisions stated in legislation and laws. The study aimed to demonstrate the ability of financial reports in the banking sector to reflect the expected results of political decisions, and to disclose them in a way that meets the needs and requirements of customers and investors for accounting information. The study relied on an analysis of the actual financial data included in the financial reports of (37) Iraqi banks listed on the Iraqi stock market during the period (2022-2024). With a total of (111) views, using three basic models to measure political decision efficiency (PDE), information transparency and disclosure (ITD), and financial report quality (FSQ), they work together to reach an accounting model based on the application of international accounting standards that discloses the effects of implementing political decisions.

title: Leeches and linchpins: a scoping review of seafood market intermediaries in small-scale fishery supply chains
summary: Abstract Seafood market intermediaries, often termed middlemen, play a crucial yet contested role in connecting small-scale fisheries (SSF) to global seafood markets. While their influence has long been recognized, scholarly accounts have tended to frame these intermediaries as either exploitative actors who constrain fishers’ livelihoods or as essential actors who provide access to markets, finance, and social protection. This scoping review examines how recent literature (2019–2021) normatively frames seafood market intermediaries, and what these framings reveal about scholarly and policy discourses on SSF. Using a qualitative synthesis of peer-reviewed and grey literature, we identify predominant framings that cast these intermediaries as both leeches and linchpins, thereby reinforcing power asymmetries while also buffering fishers against economic and social risks. We discuss how these normative framings shape broader narratives that influence fisheries governance and policy, with implications for equitable outcomes. The paper also demonstrates the value of systematic scoping methods for synthesizing qualitative marine social science research and provides methodological reflections for small research teams. Recognizing the diverse, gendered, and socially embedded roles of intermediaries can inform more just and context-sensitive interventions in SSF seafood supply chains.

title: Digital Traceability, Consumer Trust, and Sustainable Value Creation in Agrifood Supply Chains
summary: The increasing complexity of agrifood supply chains has intensified demands for transparency, food safety, product authenticity, and sustainability. Digital traceability connects information across supply chain stages through technologies such as blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), QR codes, and digital information systems. This study examines the role of digital traceability in strengthening consumer trust and supporting sustainable value creation in agrifood supply chains. A qualitative Systematic Literature Review (SLR) analyzed 15 scientific articles published between 2022 and 2024. Articles were selected from academic databases using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and analyzed through thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that digital traceability improves transparency by increasing the availability and verifiability of product origin information. Reliable traceability information can reduce information asymmetry and strengthen consumer confidence in food safety, product authenticity, and sustainability attributes. Consumer trust links traceability information with purchasing decisions, willingness to pay, and acceptance of sustainable food products. Digital traceability also supports sustainable value creation through improved accountability, information exchange, stakeholder coordination, and reduced opportunities for food fraud. However, implementation remains constrained by technology costs, data quality, interoperability, digital literacy, governance, and unequal access among smallholders. The review concludes that digital traceability can support sustainable agrifood supply chains when combined with reliable data, stakeholder collaboration, inclusive governance, and effective consumer communication. Institutional support and stakeholder engagement remain essential for strengthening consumer trust and promoting sustainable value creation.

title: The Influence of Human Capital and AKHLAK Culture on Employee Performance through Good Corporate Governance
summary: This study aims to examine the Influence of Human Capital and AKHLAK Culture on Employee Performance through Good Corporate Governance at Bank Mandiri Parepare Area.
