title: Governing for sustainability in a dynamic environment: the roles of corporate governance, organizational capabilities and entrepreneurial culture in Indonesian rural banks
summary: This study examines the determinants of sustainable performance among Indonesian Rural Banks (BPRs) by integrating Information Technology Adoption (IT), Internal Control (IC), Human Capital Capability (HC), and Good Corporate Governance (GCG), while examining Environmental Dynamism (ED) as a moderating condition. Using a quantitative approach, the study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with data from 436 BPR respondents and a second-order construct specification. The findings show that Internal Control and Human Capital Capability have significant positive effects on BPR Sustainable Performance, whereas Information Technology Adoption has no significant direct effect. Information Technology Adoption and Internal Control significantly influence GCG, while Human Capital Capability does not. GCG has a significant positive effect on Sustainable Performance and selectively mediates the effects of Information Technology Adoption and Internal Control, but not Human Capital Capability. Environmental Dynamism positively moderates the relationship between GCG and Sustainable Performance. The study contributes to the sustainable performance literature by integrating technological, organizational, governance, and environmental perspectives within a unified second-order PLS-SEM framework. The findings demonstrate that technology adoption alone does not guarantee sustainable performance; its contribution is more effectively realized when supported by effective governance and organizational control mechanisms.

title: Governance Structures Mechanisms and Sustainability Reporting Clarity: Stakeholder Dialogue as a Catalyst
summary: Growing societal demands for corporate accountability have increased pressure on companies, particularly in the energy sector, to provide transparent sustainability reporting. This study examines the effects of good corporate governance mechanisms institutional ownership, managerial ownership, independent commissioners, audit committees, and the board of directors on sustainability report disclosure, with stakeholder engagement as a moderating variable. This study employed a quantitative research approach using an explanatory design with panel data from 79 Indonesian energy companies (316 firm-year observations) during 2019–2022. The data were analyzed using Moderated Multiple Regression (MMR). The results indicate that institutional ownership has a significant negative effect on sustainability report disclosure (b = −3.2571; p = 0.020), while the other governance variables have no significant direct effects. Stakeholder engagement significantly moderates the relationship between institutional ownership and sustainability report disclosure (b = 0.4027; p = 0.022) but does not significantly moderate the remaining governance mechanisms. These findings highlight the importance of stakeholder engagement in strengthening the role of institutional investors in promoting sustainability reporting transparency in emerging economies.

title: Employee Legal Protection in the Digital Economy: A Bibliometric and Systematic Review
summary: This study examined how research on employee legal protection had developed and how far it had absorbed the governance problems created by digitally mediated work. A hybrid design combining bibliometric performance analysis, term co-occurrence mapping, and systematic review procedures was applied to 2,253 Scopus-indexed records published between 1955 and 2026 and retrieved in September 2026. Topical precision was assessed using a relevance-coded random sample of 200 records, while performance indicators were recomputed for journals-only and high-precision subsets. Output grew at an annual rate of approximately ten per cent between 1995 and 2025, yet the field remained highly fragmented: 94.3 per cent of 4,385 authors contributed only one document, author productivity followed a Lotka exponent of 4.2, and source distribution departed from Bradford’s law. Only 37 per cent of sampled records were core to the topic. Digital themes rose from below 2.5 per cent before 2015 to 23.0 per cent in 2025, while occupational safety declined in relative share. After age normalisation, digital-theme documents were cited above the field average. The findings showed a shift from physical and contractual risks toward informational and algorithmic risks, supporting compliance design for platform-based ventures. This study offered the first field-level bibliometric map of employee legal protection and quantified its digital reorientation.

title: Carbon Accounting Disclosures Effect on the Firm Value of Listed Consumer Goods Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of carbon accounting information disclosure on the market valuation of listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria for the period 2016–2025. Specifically, the study investigated the effects of carbon emission disclosure, carbon reduction and mitigation disclosure, and carbon-related risk and management disclosure on market valuation. An ex-post facto research design was adopted, while secondary data was obtained from the annual reports, sustainability reports and audited financial statements of sampled listed consumer goods firms. Market valuation was measured using Tobin’s Q, while the explanatory variables were measured using disclosure indices. Panel regression analysis was employed to test the hypotheses at the 5% level of significance. The findings revealed that carbon emission disclosure had a positive and significant effect on market valuation (β = 0.218; p = 0.004). Carbon reduction and mitigation disclosure also had a positive and significant effect on market valuation (β = 0.267; p = 0.001), while carbon-related risk and management disclosure exerted a positive and significant effect on market valuation (β = 0.193; p = 0.014). The study concludes that carbon accounting information constitutes value-relevant information to investors in the Nigerian consumer goods sector. It recommends that listed firms improve the quality and comprehensiveness of carbon-related disclosures and that regulatory authorities strengthen climate-related reporting requirements and assurance mechanisms. The study contributes to the emerging literature on carbon accounting and corporate valuation by providing sector-specific evidence from an emerging capital market.

title: Hybrid SEM–ANN Reveals Nonlinear Mechanisms in Multidimensional Supply Chain Collaboration
summary: Background: Collaborative logistics strategies are vital in today’s business world, where logistics factors play a fundamental role in achieving success and sustainability. This study aims to use a hybrid SEM–ANN approach to reveal nonlinear mechanisms in multidimensional supply chain collaboration among Sudanese manufacturing companies. Methods: The current study used a descriptive methodology to examine the relationships between variables. A survey was the main data-gathering tool for a cross-sectional, non-probability sample of 246 manufacturing companies. A two-stage SEM–ANN approach was used for data analysis. Results: The findings confirm a partially positive relationship between supply chain collaborative strategy and the logistics relationship satisfaction of Sudanese manufacturing companies. The results indicate that commitment (β = 0.447, p < 0.001) and partnership (β = 0.282, p < 0.01) significantly influence information sharing. Information sharing positively affects relationship satisfaction (β = 0.04, p < 0.001). Information sharing partially mediates the relationship between collaboration dimensions and relationship satisfaction, while relationship quality exerts a significant negative moderating effect (β = −0.090, p = 0.036). The ANN analysis further confirms the relative importance of commitment as the most influential predictor. Conclusions: The dual-method approach of SEM and ANN captures both the linear mechanisms through which commitment and partnership act (SEM) and the nonlinear patterns of predictor importance (ANN).

title: Digital Transformation and Cost of Fund Efficiency: An Analysis of Liquidity and CASA Management Strategies in Islamic Banking
summary: Contemporary banking digital transformation requires Islamic banks to overhaul their liability and liquidity management strategies to achieve cost of fund efficiency. This study aims to synthesize recent literature on the relationship between digital transformation, cost of fund efficiency, and Current Account Saving Account (CASA) management in Islamic banking. The method employed is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) using the PRISMA protocol across global and national databases (2021–2026), yielding 20 final articles after a rigorous selection process and quality appraisal using the CASP instrument. The thematic synthesis results indicate that digital acceleration successfully boosts CASA collection volumes based on the Wadiah contract; however, it simultaneously triggers high fund volatility and increased customer acquisition costs. Empirically, cost of fund efficiency requires the integration of Cash Management System (CMS) ecosystems and disciplined maintenance of the Financing to Deposit Ratio (FDR) within a prudent zone to mitigate asset-liability mismatch risks driven by rate-sensitive digital depositors. From a maqashid shariah perspective, optimizing digital liquidity management must be grounded in prudence and distributive justice to shield Islamic banks from destructive rate wars and foster sustainable financial stability. Practically, these findings urge regulatory authorities (OJK/BI) to standardize digital liquidity stress-testing models, while guiding Islamic bank management (e.g., BSI) to shift focus from costly retail yield competition toward corporate Wadiah Cash Management System (CMS) ecosystems.

title: Trustworthy Electronic Business Collaboration in Supply Chain Finance: A Convergent Architecture of Distributed Ledgers, Privacy-Preserving Computation, Trusted Execution, and Digital Credentials
summary: Supply chain finance (SCF) promises to convert the creditworthiness of large anchor buyers into liquidity for their smaller suppliers, yet in practice the same information asymmetries that create the financing gap also prevent its closure. This paper argues that the binding constraint is no longer the availability of digital technology but the absence of an assurance architecture capable of making a receivable verifiable, singular, and enforceable across organisational and jurisdictional boundaries. We develop and defend a convergent architecture—here termed TCCE (Trust Anchor, Credential, Confidential Computing, and Execution layers)—that composes four technological families rather than treating them as substitutes: permissioned distributed ledgers and smart contracts as a shared registry and deterministic state machine; privacy-preserving computation (secure multi-party computation, federated learning, homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs) as the mechanism that keeps raw commercial and personal data inside its originating domain; trusted computing (hardware roots of trust, remote attestation, trusted execution environments) as the mechanism that makes computation itself auditable; and digital credentials (decentralised identifiers, verifiable credentials, reliable electronic signatures, and electronic transferable records) as the bridge between cryptographic state and legal fact. Using accounts-receivable electronic certificates (ARECs) in China as the empirical setting—an instrument whose outstanding balance reached RMB 2.75 trillion and whose financing balance reached RMB 2.08 trillion in the first quarter of 2026 under a newly tightened regulatory regime—we show that duplicate financing, unverifiable trade backgrounds, failed credit pass-through, and cross-platform non-interoperability are four manifestations of a single underlying defect: the absence of a continuously verifiable link between a business event, a legal right, and a payment obligation. We formalize this defect, derive conditions under which verifiable disclosure strictly dominates both full concealment and full disclosure, specify an implementation blueprint with lifecycle controls, and evaluate the architecture against a stated adversary model, Chinese and international compliance requirements, and unit-economics constraints. The paper contributes a design theory for trustworthy inter-organisational collaboration that is simultaneously technically executable, legally grounded, and economically sustainable, and it identifies why a substantial share of prior trade-finance consortia failed on governance and adoption rather than on cryptography.

title: Improving the Organizational and Methodological Mechanisms for Formulating Accounting Policies and Strengthening Accounting Controls in Agricultural Enterprises
summary: This study examines the organizational and methodological mechanisms for formulating accounting policies and strengthening accounting controls in agricultural enterprises. The research employs comparative analysis, documentary examination, systematic assessment, and conceptual modelling to identify existing accounting challenges and develop recommendations for their improvement. Based on the available case materials relating to “Tarakkiyot” farm in Nishon district, Kashkadarya region, Uzbekistan, the study identifies key priorities for improving primary accounting documentation, crop-specific analytical accounting, document circulation, and inventory verification. An integrated organizational and methodological framework is proposed to coordinate accounting-policy formulation, transaction recording, internal control procedures, and financial reporting. The scientific contribution of the study lies in developing a systematic approach that integrates accounting methods and control mechanisms while considering the specific characteristics of agricultural production. The findings provide a methodological foundation for enhancing the reliability, transparency, and managerial usefulness of accounting information in agricultural enterprises. The proposed framework requires further empirical validation.

title: From ESG Performance to New Quality Productive Forces: The Role of Sustained Investor Attention
summary: ESG standards are becoming increasingly important for firms seeking to enhance productive capabilities while pursuing sustainable development. However, limited evidence exists on whether ESG performance is associated with firms’ new quality productive forces (NQPF) and on how investors’ sustained engagement with firm-specific information shapes this relationship. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2024, this study examines the relationship between ESG performance and NQPF, with particular attention to the moderating role of sustained investor attention. The results show that ESG performance is positively associated with firms’ NQPF, and this finding remains robust after addressing potential endogeneity and conducting a series of robustness checks. More importantly, sustained investor attention strengthens the positive relationship between ESG performance and NQPF. This reinforcing effect is more pronounced among larger firms, firms located in more market-oriented regions, and firms facing greater financing constraints. Further analysis shows that corporate greenwashing is associated with lower sustained investor attention, consistent with the view that greenwashing undermines the credibility and informational value of ESG-related information and weakens investors’ incentives to maintain continued engagement with such information. These findings extend the literature on the economic consequences of ESG and highlight sustained investor attention as an important capital market condition shaping the relationship between ESG performance and firms’ productive transformation.

title: What 1,067 World Bank Audit Reports Reveal About Control and Corruption Risk
summary: This paper reviews the 1,067 audit reports on World Bank-financed projects published in 2026 for Western and Central Africa, Eastern and Southern Africa, and the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region. 200 reports contained internal-control findings, from which 1,192 findings were coded to a fixed taxonomy of control categories, risk levels and corruption-risk mechanisms. Most weaknesses concern routine transactions: expenditure without supporting documents, advances left unsettled, unreconciled bank accounts and missing asset registers. Expenditure tracking and financial reporting account for 26% of all findings and 52% of those rated critical. About half of the findings (592) describe a weakness that could allow fraud, diversion or favouritism, most often through spending that was not verified or was ineligible. Other recurring issues are procurement weaknesses during contract execution, project closure, unpaid taxes and social charges, weak internal audit and prior-year findings that remain uncorrected. Only one published report in five contains internal-control findings, largely because the management letter is usually not included in the published PDF. The paper proposes five indicators for monitoring between audits. Risk levels and corruption-risk ratings are the author's assessment and indicate exposure, not proven cases.

title: Fintech at work: examining the psychological mechanisms linking fintech use and work productivity in the financial industry
summary: Drawing on a survey of 934 Chinese finance employees, this study examines the association of fintech use with employees’ psychological conditions and work productivity in the financial industry. Using Kahn’s (1990) work engagement framework, we analyze how fintech use relates to psychological meaningfulness, safety, and availability and how these conditions influence employees’ perceived productivity gains that are attributable to fintech usage. The study also explores how the openness to change moderates the relationships between fintech use and these psychological dimensions among employees. The data were analyzed using partial least squares (PLS). The results show that fintech use is associated with a reduction in psychological meaningfulness and safety but an enhancement in psychological availability. These outcomes may stem from the reduction in task significance and psychological meaningfulness driven by core task automation, the undermining of psychological safety via system complexity, and the freeing up of employee resources through streamlined workflows to enhance psychological availability. In addition, employees with higher levels of psychological meaningfulness, safety, and availability have greater work productivity (R² value = 0.467). The relationship between fintech use and work productivity is fully mediated by psychological meaningfulness, safety, and availability. Moreover, openness to change intensifies the psychological effects of fintech use, amplifying the negative impact on psychological meaningfulness while reinforcing the positive effect on psychological availability. These findings highlight the asymmetric psychological consequences of fintech adoption and underscore their implications for enhancing employee productivity in the financial sector.

title: Time-Series modeling of supply chain disruption drivers in ASEAN agri-food logistics networks
summary: Disruptions in agri-food supply chains pose logistical and operational challenges for ASEAN member economies, whose agricultural sectors are simultaneously exposed to fluctuations in freight costs and climate-related production shocks. Prior time-series applications in shipping markets, agricultural commodity co-movement, and supply chain performance have generally examined these channels separately, and the joint transmission of these channels into ASEAN agri-food commodity logistics outcomes remains largely unexamined. This study applies a Vector Autoregression (VAR) time-series modeling framework to identify and quantify the principal drivers of disruption in ASEAN agri-food logistics networks, using 4,108 daily observations spanning January 2015 to March 2026. Seven variables are jointly modeled: Baltic Dry Index daily change (D_BDI), Brent crude oil log-return (R_Brent), Geopolitical Risk Index daily change (D_GPR), Oceanic Niño Index anomaly change (D_ONI), ASEAN aggregate agricultural production return (R_ASEAN_Production), and daily price changes of Robusta and Arabica coffee. Stationarity is verified by the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests. The lag order p = 2 is selected based on BIC and HQIC. GPR shocks exert statistically significant lagged effects on Arabica price (p = 0.007) and Robusta price (p = 0.021); ONI anomaly changes significantly propagate into Robusta prices (p = 0.021). A cross-domain pathway from ONI to GPR (p = 0.010) is consistent with climate disruption signals coinciding with subsequent geopolitical risk movements. BDI first-order persistence coefficient is 0.596 (p < 0.001). Forecast Error Variance Decomposition (FEVD) shows Robusta-to-Arabica cross-variance at 44.03% at horizon 10. Durbin-Watson statistics (1.958–2.061) confirm residual white noise across all equations. These results provide quantitative inputs for engineering early-warning systems for disruption and logistics resilience planning in ASEAN agri-food supply networks.

title: Harmonization of Islamic Financial Accounting Standards: A Comparison of the Domestic PSAK Framework and International AAOIFI Standards
summary: The harmonization of Islamic financial accounting standards is an absolute prerequisite for creating transparency, accountability, and comparability of financial reports of Islamic financial institutions in the global arena. This study aims to synthesize contemporary literature regarding the comparison between the domestic Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (PSAK) framework and international accounting standards issued by the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI). The method employed is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) using the PRISMA protocol across global and national databases for the 2021–2026 period, yielding 20 final articles after rigorous selection and CASP quality assessment. The thematic synthesis results indicate that although domestic PSAK has adopted certain IFRS convergence principles, significant harmonization gaps remain, particularly regarding accounting treatment for risk-sharing investment instruments, fair value measurement, revenue recognition, and the classification of Restricted Investment Accounts / Temporary Syirkah Funds (DST). Empirically, these jurisdictional differences and standard interpretations trigger high compliance costs for multinational Islamic banks. From the perspective of Islamic accounting and muamalah fatwas, harmonization based on maqashid syariah is essential to ensure information honesty (shidq), fair presentation (‘adalah), and the protection of stakeholders' rights.

title: Analysis of the Accounting Information System for the Sales and Cash Receipts Cycle in Enhancing Internal Control at PT Asia Raya Technology Medan
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of the accounting information system in the sales and cash receipts cycle to enhance internal control at PT Asia Raya Technology Medan. A qualitative approach with a descriptive case study method was employed. Data were collected through interviews, observations, documentation, and literature review, and analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing techniques. The findings indicate that the accounting information system has supported sales and cash receipts activities through computerized transaction recording, faster financial reporting, and the implementation of internal control mechanisms, including segregation of duties, transaction authorization, and restricted system access. However, several weaknesses were identified, such as inconsistent authorization procedures, occasional data entry errors, and the absence of an independent internal audit function. This study provides insights into the importance of integrating accounting information systems with internal control to improve transaction management effectiveness in technology-based companies.

title: Taxation of the Digital Economy in Nigeria as a Tool for Economic Development: Challenges and Prospect
summary: This paper examines taxation of the digital services under Nigeria’s new tax regime as a tool for economic development, with specific focus on the legal, institutional, administrative, and international challenges affecting effective taxation of the digital economy. The growth of digital platforms and cross-border online transactions has transformed commercial activities and created significant revenue opportunities for governments. However, traditional tax rules especially in less developed nations have struggled to capture income generated through digital presence without physical establishment. Nigeria tackled this issue through intermittent Finance Acts and the recent tax reforms, incorporating measures aimed at expanding the tax net to digital service providers. The study aimed at critically analysing taxation of digital services under Nigeria’s new tax regime and evaluating the challenges confronting effective implementation. The objectives of the paper include the examination of the legal framework regulating digital taxation in Nigeria, analysis of jurisdictional and enforcement challenges, and assessment of international standards influencing digital taxation in Nigeria. The study adopts a doctrinal research methodology. Primary sources consulted include statutes, international conventions, regulations, and judicial authorities, while secondary sources consulted include textbooks, journal articles, reports, and internet materials. Findings from the paper reveals that Nigeria has so far made significant progress through introduction of new tax legislations and alignment with emerging global tax standards. However, the absence of clear enforcement mechanisms, limited international cooperation, technological limitations, and the historical inconsistencies in tax administration continue to hinder the overall effectiveness of taxation in Nigeria as a tool for development. Clear jurisdictional rules, stronger international cooperation, improved technological capacity for tax authorities, harmonisation of tax administration procedures, and continuous review of digital tax policies are recommended to be put in place in order to reflect evolving technological advancements for optimum performance and development in Nigeria.

title: Earnings Management and Future Dividend Pay-out: A Study of Listed Non-financial Firms in Nigeria
summary: This scholarly inquiry examines the extent to which earnings management practices exert influence over subsequent dividend disbursements within a cohort of 32 non-financial corporations listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, spanning the period from 2020 to 2023. Employing panel data analysis, the investigation assessed the repercussions of both accrual-based and real earnings management, while simultaneously controlling for variables such as current dividend payout, earnings per share (EPS), liquidity, firm size, and leverage. Descriptive statistical analysis indicated considerable heterogeneity in dividend payouts among the sampled firms. A fixed-effects model, corroborated by the Hausman test, was utilised for the regression analysis, producing an R-squared value of 0.457, which suggests a moderate degree of explanatory capability. The principal findings reveal that neither category of earnings management, discretionary accruals (p = 0.8154) nor real activities manipulation (p = 0.2215), exerts a statistically significant influence on forthcoming dividends, thereby necessitating the rejection of the study's principal hypotheses. In contrast, the decisions regarding dividends were chiefly influenced by fundamental financial indicators: EPS exhibited a robust positive correlation (β = 0.439, p = 0.0001), leverage demonstrated a significant adverse relationship (β = -0.694, p = 0.0397), and liquidity also presented a positive and significant effect (p = 0.0486). The study concludes that, within the Nigerian context, earnings management fails to serve as a dependable predictor of dividends. It underscores the imperative for corporations to focus on genuine profitability and prudent financial governance, and it advocates for enhanced regulatory oversight to facilitate transparent reporting, thereby safeguarding investor interests and promoting sustainable dividend policies.

summary: A fintech engineering whitepaper on layered wallet architecture, Rust at the ledger, and why boring is the only property that scales with AI Joel Alcarez · October 2026 Abstract | People make slop without understanding the codebase. It is deliberately unfashionable. No ORM on the money path, no reflection, no microservice per noun. The goal is that a new engineer can trace a dollar from request torow in five minutes. 1. The Law, Updated for 2026Spolsky's original formulation was about TCP pretending to be reliable, SQL pretending to be declarative, and file systems pretending to be local. The abstractions were written by humans, so someone usually understood the failure mode, even if the user did not. | The Law of Leaky Abstractions, 2026 edition:| Every AI-generated abstraction leaks,and you won't know where until it costs you money.The update is not that AI code is worse than human code. It is that the author no longer holds the mental model of the leak.When a human writes a wrapper, they usually knowwhich edge they skipped. When a model writes it, nobody does, and the code is fluent enough that review attention drops exactly when it should rise. We call the cost of closing that gap the abstraction tax: the review time, test infrastructure, type design, and incident response you pay to find a leak before production finds it for you. You cannot avoid the tax. You can only choose where to pay it and in what currency. In most software the currency is a bad afternoon. In a ledger the currency is dollars, and the bill arrives with an audit trail attached. The rest of this paper is about paying the tax early, cheaply, and in the right layer.

title: Practice of Digital Transformation of Intelligent Education Management in Higher Vocational Colleges
summary: Wisdom drives the transformation of higher vocational governance, but process fragmentation, data islands, and lagging performance hinder the change. This study relies on 850,000 multi-source logs from two provincial higher vocational colleges from 2019 to 2024 to build a “business-data” dual-loop model. The authors optimize the closed-loop of approval and strengthen real-time quality inspection and analysis. Empirical evidence shows that the longer the approval chain, the more frequent the rework. Experiments show that the approval time is reduced, and the satisfaction is increased. The authors innovatively design a three-layer five-dimensional indicator system and a dual-loop state machine and embed interpretable AI feedback to form a generalizable precise governance paradigm.

title: The Heterogeneous Impacts of Digital Transformation on Firms’ Internationalization: Evidence from China
summary: Using Chinese A-share-listed firms from 2013 to 2023, this study examines whether and how digital transformation affects firm internationalization. We measure internationalization along both the intensive and extensive margins, including overseas revenue share, overseas operating revenue, internationalization participation, and a BERT-based internationalization indicator constructed from annual reports. Digital transformation is mainly measured by firms’ digital intangible assets, and we further use digital patents, digital job postings, and annual-report digital keyword disclosure as alternative measures. The results show that digital transformation significantly promotes firm internationalization. A one-unit increase in the digital transformation is associated with a 1.3-percentage-point higher probability of internationalization and a 0.8-percentage-point higher overseas revenue share. Further analysis based on the Awareness-Motivation-Capability (AMC) framework shows that digital transformation promotes internationalization by improving firms’ awareness of overseas opportunities, strengthening their motivation to expand abroad, and enhancing their capabilities through higher productivity and lower financing constraints. The effect is more pronounced among firms with higher initial productivity, suggesting that preexisting capabilities affect how firms convert digital investment into international expansion. Evidence from recruitment data further shows that digital transformation is associated with higher demand for highly educated workers, indicating that human-capital upgrading is an important part of this process. Overall, this study provides firm-level evidence that digital transformation supports Chinese firms’ internationalization by improving both market expansion and organizational capabilities.

title: Improving the Recognition, Classification, and Accounting of Assets and Capital Investments in Accordance With International Standards
summary: This study examines the recognition, classification, measurement, and accounting treatment of investment-related assets and capital investments in accordance with International financial reporting standards (IFRS). The research employs comparative analysis, systematic analysis, synthesis, and logical generalization to identify methodological differences between international standards and national accounting practices in Uzbekistan. Particular attention is given to investment property, long-term biological assets, right-of-use assets, and the capitalization of related expenditures. The study proposes improvements to the national chart of accounts, including the modification of existing accounts and the introduction of additional analytical accounts for specific asset categories. The proposed methodological framework aims to enhance the accuracy of asset classification, strengthen accounting controls over capital investments, and improve the transparency, reliability, and comparability of financial reporting.

title: Perceived Tariff Policy Uncertainty and Logistics Cost Pressure: The Mediating Role of Supply Chain Adjustment in Vietnam
summary: This study examines the relationship between perceived tariff policy uncertainty (TU), supply chain adjustment intensity (SCA), and logistics cost pressure (LCP) among firms engaged in seaborne import and export activities in Vietnam. Drawing on transaction cost economics, real options theory, and the dynamic capabilities perspective, the study proposes that tariff policy uncertainty affects logistics cost pressure both directly and indirectly through firms’ supply chain adjustments. Data were collected from 320 valid firm-level survey responses across three regions of Vietnam and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). TU and LCP were specified as reflective constructs, whereas SCA was modelled formatively. The results show that TU is positively associated with SCA and LCP, while SCA is positively associated with LCP. The indirect effect of TU on LCP through SCA is also positive and significant, indicating complementary partial mediation. The model explains 33.7% of the variance in SCA and 42.0% in LCP and demonstrates positive out-of-sample predictive relevance. The findings suggest that tariff uncertainty generates logistics cost pressure not only through uncertainty itself but also through the organizational costs associated with supply chain reconfiguration. The study contributes to the trade-policy and logistics literature by identifying supply chain adjustment as an important transmission mechanism in an emerging-market context.

title: Digitalization is More Than Just a Trend: Modernizing Financial Reporting in the Halal MSME Ecosystem of the Riau Islands
summary: This study examines the modernization of financial reporting among MSMEs in Riau Islands Province, focusing on Ayuraskitchen, a home-based business in Batam City that has grown into a multi-outlet cake business. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the study analyzes the gradual transition in financial reporting from manual records and Microsoft Excel templates to the Lamikro application and, ultimately, the digital accounting application Mekari Jurnal. The findings indicate that modernization occurred gradually in accordance with the growth and needs of the business and was supported by consistent record-keeping, government training and assistance, and the availability of accessible technology. The implementation of digital financial reporting improved the organization, efficiency, and accessibility of financial information, while supporting cash flow monitoring and faster business decision-making. Systematic financial records also help MSMEs prepare financing documentation and improve their bankability by providing more structured business information, although access to financing is influenced by other factors. The study recommends strengthening accounting and digital literacy, providing continuous assistance, implementing SAK EMKM, and fostering collaboration among MSMEs, local governments, financial institutions, and financial technology providers to accelerate the modernization of MSME financial reporting.
